title: RBAC v2 authorization handshake, phased migration and customer transition notice
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket coordinates the final staged migration of account authorization from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 across Redwood production. It covers the dual-write period, background backfill strategy, audit log verification, SSO/SAML mapping validation, canary rollout, automated sanity checks, customer communication plan, and explicit rollback triggers.

Motivation / goals:
- Move all accounts to RBAC v2 while preserving access semantics and audit continuity.
- Enable a dual-write window so tenants continue to operate if one system falls behind.
- Provide visibility (dashboards + alerts) so on-call can detect divergence early.
- Minimize customer-facing disruption and provide a clear support playbook.

Scope:
- Code changes: API layer dual-write (v1 + v2), feature flag gate for reads, migration worker for backfills, admin console upgrade for role mapping, audit-log adapter that stamps origin version.
- Verification: daily reconciliation, sampled policy evals, SSO mapping smoke tests per IdP.
- Communication: targeted email to customers with custom RBAC mappings and a public change note for self-serve tenants.

High-level approach / run stages:
1) Pre-cutover validation (now): generate reconciliation baseline between v1 and v2 for all active tenants (last 90 days). Create per-tenant divergence report in BigQuery.
2) Dual-write enablement (flagged): writes go to both systems. Reads continue to use v1 by default. Feature flag: rbac_v2_dualwrite.
3) Canary reads (traffic-split): enable read verification for 5% of requests (routed internally) to compare v1 vs v2 decisions in realtime. Log disagreements to a debug topic and an Alerting dashboard.
4) Progressive read migration: move small cohorts (internal teams -> low-risk customers -> high-usage customers) to reads from v2.
5) Backfill completion: run high-throughput idempotent backfill worker until queue empty; mark tenant as "v2-synced".
6) Cutover and deprecate v1 reads after 4 weeks of stable metrics; final audit export; archival of v1 decision store.

Backfill strategy (detailed):
- Worker: idempotent, resumable, partitioned by tenant_id. Each job writes role bindings into v2 and emits event to audit topic.
- Batch sizing: start with 500 accounts/sec/worker; monitor 95th latency on write paths and DB replication lag. Scale down if p50 write latency > 200ms or replication lag > 30s.
- Resume tokens: persist last_processed_id per tenant in migration_state table.
- Data integrity checks: hash(role_list_v1) -> compare to hash(role_list_v2) after write; retry on mismatch up to 3 times. Failed tenant goes to manual reconciliation queue.
- Example backfill SQL (for review):
  -- snapshot candidate roles from v1 store
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, ARRAY_AGG(role) as roles_v1
  FROM authorizations_v1
  WHERE updated_at > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 2 YEAR)
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id;

Dual-write mechanics and trade-offs:
- We will write all new role changes to both v1 and v2. Advantages: minimal immediate customer impact and ability to rollback by switching reads. Disadvantages: higher write amplification and transient divergence risk during backfill.
- To reduce divergence we will: make writes sequential with per-entity causal ordering (write v2 then v1) and include write_id monotonic token to detect missing sequences. If v1 write fails, enqueue corrective job; if v2 write fails, block request (v2 is authoritative for new accounts).

SSO/SAML / role mapping validation:
- Create an automated smoke test harness that: performs SAML login against each configured IdP test endpoint, asserts group->role mapping into v2, and confirms session permissions.
- For customers with custom mapping logic, create a mapping-audit export and run sampled policy evals on production samples (stored in a secure GCS path).

Audit logging and observability:
- Audit records must include: actor, action, resource, old_roles, new_roles, origin_version (v1|v2), request_id, timestamp.
- Add a new "rbac_migration" field to audit events to indicate phase and whether event was generated by backfill, manual change, or dual-write.
- Dashboards/alerts:
  - Divergence rate (disagreements/vs-evaluations) > 0.1% -> P1 alert.
  - Backfill failure rate > 0.5% for 15m -> P0 alert.
  - Avg API decision latency increase > +30ms baseline for 10m -> P1 alert.
- Expose a per-tenant migration status page in Console and an internal table for on-call.

Canary and rollback triggers:
- Canary window metrics to observe for 60 minutes: divergence, auth latency, downstream errors (403 anomalies), audit event lag.
- Automatic rollback triggers (immediate):
  - Canary divergence > 0.5% for any 10m window AND affected requests include admin or system roles.
  - P50 decision latency > 500ms OR P95 > 1s for the auth path.
  - Backfill queue processing rate drops by >70% for 30m with queue size growing.
- Manual rollback path: toggle feature flag to route reads back to v1 and pause backfill workers. Notify customers and start incident bridge.

Customer communication plan:
- Tiered notices: 2-week advance email to high-privilege tenants with mapping preview; 72-hour email to self-serve customers; UI banner in Console for affected tenants.
- Support playbook and pre-written email templates stored in Confluence (link in links field).
- Office hours: schedule two migration office-hour sessions (one APAC, one NA/EU) the week of cutover.

Open questions & decisions to capture:
- Decision: v2 becomes authoritative for new writes during dual-write window (approved by SecOps 2025-10-28).
- Question: should we include read-repair on every auth check when mismatch detected (tradeoff: extra latency vs. faster consistency)? Current plan: do not repair on read path; emit event and enqueue async repair.

Artifacts and references:
- Confluence migration spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Migration+Spec
- Draft external notice (docs): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-migration-notice
- GH PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4892 (dual-write), https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4921 (backfill worker)
- BigQuery reconciliation job: project:infra-metrics.dataset.rbac_reconciliation_2025

Acceptance criteria (done):
- Dual-write flag implemented and tested in staging.
- Canary reads running with disagreement logging and dashboard.
- Backfill worker tested end-to-end with resume tokens and idempotency.
- Audit events include origin_version and rbac_migration tag.
- Customer comms drafted, approved by legal, and scheduled.

Post-migration follow-ups:
- Run full export of audit trail for compliance (retain 2 years).
- Deprecate and archive v1 decision store after a 30-day observation window.
- Postmortem and lessons learned document with metrics and cost impact.
